    """Create geometries from the Well-Known Text (WKT) representation.

    with pytest.raises(shapely.GEOSException, match="Points of LinearRing do not form a closed linestring"):

    poly_wkt = "POLYGON ((0 0, 1 0, 1 1, 0 1))"  # missing closing 0 0
    expected = Polygon([(0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1)])
    actual = shapely.from_wkt(poly_wkt, strict=False)
    assert_geometries_equal(actual, expected)

    poly_wkt = "POLYGON ((0 0, 1 0, 1 1, 0 1))"
    expected = Polygon([(0, 0), (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 1)])
    actual = shapely.from_wkt(poly_wkt, fix_structure=True)

    actual = wkt_loads(poly_wkt, strict=False)

def test_from_wkt_strict_false_repairs_nested_unclosed_polygon():
    gc_wkt = "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION (POLYGON ((0 0, 1 0, 1 1, 0 1)))"
    actual = shapely.from_wkt(gc_wkt, strict=False)

def _fix_polygon_rings(poly_coords: str) -> str:
    # poly_coords includes outer parentheses, eg: "((...),(...))"
    # We walk through and fix each inner ring
    result_chars = []
    i = 0
    n = len(poly_coords)
    while i < n:
        ch = poly_coords[i]
        result_chars.append(ch)
        if ch == "(":
            # start of a ring; capture until matching ')'
            depth = 1
            start = i + 1
            i += 1
            while i < n and depth > 0:
                if poly_coords[i] == "(":
                    depth += 1
                elif poly_coords[i] == ")":
                    depth -= 1
                i += 1
            end = i - 1  # position of the matching ')'
            ring_content = poly_coords[start:end]
            # Only process if this was a single-level ring (no nested parentheses inside)
            if "(" not in ring_content and ")" not in ring_content:
                parts = [p.strip() for p in ring_content.split(",") if p.strip()]
                if len(parts) >= 2:
                    first = parts[0]
                    last = parts[-1]
                    if _normalize_coord_string(first) != _normalize_coord_string(last):
                        # append first to close the ring
                        ring_content = ", ".join(parts + [first])

                # remove the previously appended '(' and everything until ')'
                # We reconstruct: '(' + ring_content + ')'
                # Remove the existing content added to result_chars after '('
                # First, remove what was appended since start
                del result_chars[-1]  # remove the '(' we added earlier
                # Add fixed ring
                result_chars.append("(")
                result_chars.append(ring_content)

def _fix_wkt_structure_scalar(wkt: str) -> str:
    # Only attempt simple structural fixes: close polygon rings
    s = wkt
    i = 0
    n = len(s)
    out = []
    while i < n:
        if s.startswith("POLYGON", i):
            out.append("POLYGON")
            i += len("POLYGON")
            # consume optional dimension tokens and whitespace
            while i < n and s[i].isspace():
                out.append(s[i]); i += 1
            # possible dimension token Z/M/ZM
            if i < n and s[i] in ("Z", "M"):
                # could be Z or M or ZM
                out.append(s[i]); i += 1
                if i < n and s[i] == "M":
                    out.append("M"); i += 1
                # consume whitespace after dimension
                while i < n and s[i].isspace():
                    out.append(s[i]); i += 1
            # check for EMPTY
            if s.startswith("EMPTY", i):
                out.append("EMPTY"); i += len("EMPTY")
                continue
            # next should be '(' starting polygon coordinates
            if i < n and s[i] == "(":
                # capture until matching ')'
                depth = 0
                start = i
                while i < n:
                    if s[i] == "(":
                        depth += 1

    """Create geometries from the Well-Known Text (WKT) representation.

    The Well-known Text format is defined in the `OGC Simple Features
    Specification for SQL <https://www.opengeospatial.org/standards/sfs>`__.

    Parameters
    ----------
    geometry : str or array_like
        The WKT string(s) to convert.
    on_invalid : {"raise", "warn", "ignore"}, default "raise"
        - raise: an exception will be raised if WKT input geometries are invalid.
        - warn: a warning will be raised and invalid WKT geometries will be
          returned as ``None``.

        (e.g., close unclosed rings) when reading WKT. This maps to
        ``fix_structure=True``.

    --------

    if not np.isscalar(on_invalid):

    invalid_handler = np.uint8(DecodingErrorOptions.get_value(on_invalid))

    # Map strict to fix_structure unless fix_structure is explicitly provided
    if fix_structure is None:
        fix_structure = not strict

    # Pre-process geometry strings if fix_structure requested
    if fix_structure:
        # ensure object dtype for element-wise processing
        arr = np.asarray(geometry, dtype=object)
        def _fix_elem(elem):

        else:

            geometry = np.vectorize(_fix_elem, otypes=[object])(arr)

    return lib.from_wkt(geometry, invalid_handler, **kwargs)
